records.title: VIC2026 – Mapping One Nation’s 2025 Federal Result
records.summary: Green maps the 2025 federal House result onto Victorian state electorates. One Nation averaged 8.2% in rural/regional seats, 6.2% in outer Melbourne and 3.5% in inner Melbourne. He explicitly presents this as geographic pattern evidence, not a 2026 vote forecast.
records.notes: Useful held-out diagnostic for the ONP geography workstream; do not multiply the mapped 2025 vote mechanically into a state-election forecast.

records.title: Victorian Upper House evenly split between L-NP/One Nation and ALP/Greens
records.summary: Roy Morgan's July–September regional survey (n=2,845) projects 12 Coalition, 10 Labor, 8 Greens and 6 One Nation Council seats, with four seats unresolved by its stated method. This supersedes the older August Roy Morgan Council snapshot as the fresher comparison.
records.notes: Reference evidence only. Regional samples are modest and the unresolved seats are material; do not manufacture a complete 40-seat allocation.

records.title: One Nation and L-NP Coalition set to win key seats of Bass, Hastings, Morwell and Pakenham
records.summary: A small Roy Morgan SMS poll of 283 electors across Bass, Hastings, Morwell and Pakenham points to Coalition/One Nation strength in all four seats. It is useful directional evidence but too small for treating the four seat calls as high-precision estimates.
records.notes: Held out from fitting. Use as external validation of geography/final-pair behaviour only, with explicit small-sample caution.
